name: אינטגרל מסוים בחלקים – t·e^(−kt) (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Evaluate the following definite integral:

\( \displaystyle \int_{{CT:0}}^{{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}\,d{{CT:3}} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Take the constant out of the integral, find an antiderivative by integration by parts, then evaluate it at the limits.
Step 1 — Linearity and integration by parts
If

\[ \int f(x) dx = F(x) \]

then

\[ \int^a_b f(x) dx = F(a) - F(b). \]

So, we need to calculate

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}}. \]

By linearity,

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:4}} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}} \]

So, using integration by parts, that is if \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of {{CT:6}} then

\[ \int u dv = uv - \int v du, \]

by defining \(u = {{CT:7}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:8}} d{{CT:3}}\) so that \(du = {{CT:9}} d{{CT:3}}\) and \(v = {{CT:10}}\). Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int {{CT:5}} d{{CT:3}} &= \int u dv \\ &= uv - \int v du \\ &= {{CT:7}}\left[{{CT:10}}\right] - \int \left[{{CT:10}}\right]\cdot \left({{CT:9}}\right) d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:11}} - \int {{CT:12}} d{{CT:3}} \\ &= {{CT:13}} \end{aligned} \]

Step 2 — Evaluating at the limits
Hence,

\[ \int {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} = {{CT:14}} = {{CT:15}} \]

Let \(F({{CT:3}}) = {{CT:15}}\) Then,

\[ \begin{aligned} \int^{{CT:1}}_{{CT:0}} {{CT:2}} d{{CT:3}} &= F({{CT:1}}) - F({{CT:0}}) \\ &= {{CT:16}} - {{CT:17}} \\ &= {{CT:18}} \end{aligned} \]

on_true.feedback: This is a definite integration problem, so your answer should be a number. This is the correct integral, but you have not evaluated it.
